record.paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Even-dimensional sphere analogue of the S2 theorem
record.original_question: For even-dimensional spheres S^{2m} with m > 1, restrict attention to unit vector fields defined on the sphere minus one point. Is the analogue of the S^2 theorem true: are the least-area unit vector fields exactly the parallel-transport vector fields?

evidence.quote: Among vector fields of constant length defined on .S 2 minus one point
whether a similar result is also true for other even dimensional spheres

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{2m} \subset \mathbb{R}^{2m+1}$ denote the round unit sphere of even dimension $2m$ with $m>1$, endowed with its standard Riemannian metric. A unit vector field on a subset $U \subseteq S^{2m}$ is a smooth section $V : U \to TS^{2m}$ with $\|V(p)\|=1$ for every $p \in U$. The image $V(U)$ is a submanifold of the unit tangent bundle $T^1 S^{2m}$, which carries the Sasaki metric induced from the Riemannian metric on $S^{2m}$. The volume (area) of $V$ is defined as the $2m$-dimensional volume of $V(U)$ with respect to the Sasaki metric; equivalently,
$$\mathrm{vol}(V) = \int_{U} \sqrt{\det\big(I + (\nabla V)^{*}(\nabla V)\big)} \, d\mathrm{vol}_{S^{2m}}.$$
Fix a point $p_0 \in S^{2m}$ and consider unit vector fields defined on $S^{2m} \setminus \{p_0\}$. A parallel-transport unit vector field is the unit vector field obtained by choosing a unit tangent vector $v \in T_{q} S^{2m}$ at some point $q \neq p_0$ and parallel-transporting it along the unique minimizing geodesic from $q$ to every other point of $S^{2m} \setminus \{p_0\}$ (equivalently, the vector fields invariant under the isotropy subgroup of $\mathrm{SO}(2m+1)$ fixing the antipodal axis through $p_0$).

Question: Among all unit vector fields defined on $S^{2m} \setminus \{p_0\}$, are the parallel-transport unit vector fields exactly the ones minimizing the volume functional above?

(For $m=1$, i.e.\ on $S^{2}$ minus one point, it is known that the parallel-transport unit vector fields are precisely the area-minimizing unit vector fields; the problem asks whether the same characterization holds for all $m>1$.)
artifact.category_tag: Volume-minimizing unit vector fields on spheres
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous problem on $S^2$ minus one point was solved (parallel-transport fields minimize area). For higher even-dimensional spheres minus a point, the question is posed as an open problem; recent work on "Vector Fields of Constant Length on Punctured Spheres" gives only partial results, and the general Gluck–Ziller-type minimization problem in dimensions $\geq 4$ remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Vector Fields of Constant Length on Punctured Spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work addresses unit vector fields defined on spheres with isolated singularities; only partial results are obtained.
status_evidence.claim: The even-dimensional analogue of the S^2 result remains an active open problem with only partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Area minimizing vector fields on round 2-sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes area-minimizing unit vector fields on the punctured 2-sphere as parallel-transport fields.
status_evidence.claim: The S^2 base case (parallel-transport fields are the minimizers on the punctured 2-sphere) is established.
